name: Read the canvas's build lifecycle: live pointers plus recent builds
description: Read the canvas's build lifecycle: live pointers plus recent builds Read the canvas's build lifecycle: live pointers plus recent builds. GET /api/projects/{project_id}/canvases/{id}/builds/
context:
GET /api/projects/{project_id}/canvases/{id}/builds/
Read the canvas's build lifecycle: live pointers plus recent builds. A publish queues a build; poll this until it is ready (the live pointer advances) or failed (fix the error diagnostics and publish again — the last good build stays live). Send the response's ETag back as If-None-Match to make the poll revalidate without a body.
Required: id (path) — A UUID string identifying this canvas.; project_id (path) — Project ID of the project you're trying to access. To find the ID of the project, make a call to /api/projects/.
Optional: scope (query) — "slim" returns only what rendering needs — the live build, the head version's builds, and anything still in flight — instead of the full recent-build history. Any other value (or none) returns the full window.; version_id (query) — Include the retained ready build for this historical source version.

name: Stage a complete source project as a draft version and build it, without publishing
description: Stage a complete source project as a draft version and build it, without publishing Stage a complete source project as a draft version and build it, without publishing. POST /api/projects/{project_id}/canvases/{id}/draft/
context:
POST /api/projects/{project_id}/canvases/{id}/draft/
Stage a complete source project as a draft version and build it, without publishing. The draft gets the same validation, versioning, and server-side build as a publish, but the canvas's head and live build never move, so nothing changes for viewers. Promote the version with `promote` to make it live. The response reports how the draft's declared capabilities widen the current head's, so growth in access can be reviewed before it ships. No version guard applies: a draft conflicts with nothing.
Required: id (path) — A UUID string identifying this canvas.; project_id (path) — Project ID of the project you're trying to access. To find the ID of the project, make a call to /api/projects/.; body (body)

description: Report a runtime error observed while rendering a canvas build Report a runtime error observed while rendering a canvas build. POST /api/projects/{project_id}/canvases/{id}/report_error/
context:
POST /api/projects/{project_id}/canvases/{id}/report_error/
Report a runtime error observed while rendering a canvas build. Files the report in the authoring task's thread (deduped per build and error type) so the canvas's agent can be asked to fix it. Reports never start an agent run by themselves — dispatch is `request_fix`. Only the error class crosses the server; full messages and stacks stay client-side because rendering sessions can carry viewer data.

description: Wake the canvas's authoring agent to fix a failing build or runtime error Wake the canvas's authoring agent to fix a failing build or runtime error. POST /api/projects/{project_id}/canvases/{id}/request_fix/
context:
POST /api/projects/{project_id}/canvases/{id}/request_fix/
Wake the canvas's authoring agent to fix a failing build or runtime error. Starts (or signals) an agent run on the authoring task, instructed to stage the fix as a draft the user reviews and promotes. This is the human-initiated dispatch step behind error reports; it spends agent compute, so it never fires automatically, and only the authoring task's creator may dispatch — the run executes with their credentials.
Required: id (path) — A UUID string identifying this canvas.; project_id (path) — Project ID of the project you're trying to access. To find the ID of the project, make a call to /api/projects/.; body (body)
